title: Google hints at New Topological Flat Transformer
summary: Discover AI walkthrough of Google DeepMind's April 18 2026 paper 'The topological trouble with the transformers'. Argues that classical feedforward transformer architectures fundamentally limit dynamic state tracking; proposes a continuous-flow-dynamics 'topological flat transformer' as the next-generation architecture, positioning it relative to Mamba (2024-2025) and linear-attention recurrent variants. Contains substrate-relevant claims about iterative latent-variable update vs sequential-dependency limits.
claims: Classical transformers' purely feedforward architecture fundamentally limits dynamic state tracking (Google DeepMind quote).
Iterative updating of latent variables reflecting an evolving interactive environment requires sequential dependencies that feedforward networks struggle to maintain.
Google DeepMind proposes a continuous-flow-dynamics architecture variant as a next-generation transformer; called 'topological flat transformer' in the video framing.
Architecture progression line: classical transformer (2017) -> Mamba/linear-attention (2024-2025) -> continuous-flow-dynamics (Google 2026).
The paper hints (per video author) that Google may be transitioning their core LLM stack (GPT-5.4/5.5/Opus-4.6/4.7-class competitors) onto a structurally different substrate.
